links.outcome: Differences in GPT-4 care plan themes across counterfactually varied patient sociodemographic attributes
links.effect: Low-income profiles less likely to include Environmental Adjustment (aRR 0.90); older profiles more likely to include Pain Management (aRR 1.33) and Family Support (aRR 1.62); lower education increased Family Support (aRR 1.10).
links.quote: Care plans generated for low-income patient profiles were less likely to include the theme Environmental Adjustment (adjusted relative risk [aRR] 0.90).

links.outcome: Expert-rated quality of generated content differences by patient sociodemographic profile
links.effect: Urban profiles had higher completeness (β=.22) and applicability (β=.14) but lower safety scores (β=-0.09); overall quality high (mean 4.47).
links.quote: However, urban profiles had higher completeness (β=.22) and applicability (β=.14) but lower safety scores (β=-0.09).

screen.reason: Empirical simulation study evaluating GPT-4-generated nursing care plans for sociodemographic bias across clinical vignettes with expert review, but does not test an organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
